title: Taiwan Plays its Chips Card - The Wire China
gist: Semicon Taiwan 2026 in Taipei drew more than 1,300 chipmakers and suppliers showing advanced packaging tools and specialized materials, and it also served as a stage for President Lai Ching-te's chip diplomacy. This is a paywalled teaser.

themes.theme: Semicon Taiwan as a chip-diplomacy stage

insights.claim: More than 1,300 chipmakers and suppliers exhibited at Semicon Taiwan in Taipei in early September 2026, with advanced packaging tools and specialized materials prominent.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: The weight on advanced packaging and materials shows where Taiwan's supply-chain bottlenecks and capex are concentrated, which bears on packaging-equipment and materials suppliers.
insights.quote: over 1,300 chipmakers and suppliers showcased their most sophisticated offerings
insights.locator: From advanced packaging tools to specialized

insights.claim: Taiwan's government, led by President Lai Ching-te at the Semicon Network Summit on September 1, 2026, is actively using the island's dominance in advanced chipmaking as a diplomatic lever.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Chip diplomacy ties Taiwan's security to foreign partners' supply chains; watch for new government-backed fab or packaging partnerships announced alongside diplomatic engagements.
insights.quote: Also on full display: the island’s chip diplomacy efforts.
insights.locator: From advanced packaging tools to specialized

insights.claim: Taiwan's dominance in advanced chipmaking is treated as an established fact, and the policy question has shifted to how the island turns that dominance into geopolitical leverage.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Frame Taiwan semiconductor exposure as a geopolitical bargaining asset as well as a cyclical tech exposure.
